A U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent shot an immigrant in New York City late

A young boy was in the man's car at the time of the shooting.
Police say the wounded man is conscious and was treated at a nearby hospital.
Steve Kastenbaum reports from New York City.
This triggered protests and calls for ICE to leave the city.
Police pushed back protesters as they surrounded a law enforcement vehicle trying to leave
Upper Manhattan where the shooting took place.
Its window had been shattered.
In a written statement, Mirza Ramamdani called the shooting "an unconscionable and incredibly

Governor Kathy Hochul said she expressed outrage in a call with President Trump.
The Department of Homeland Security said in a statement that ICE agents were attempting

For NPR News, I'm Steve Kastenbaum in New York.
A top Democratic senator is warning the Iran war is spiraling out of control.
Chris Murphy is back from a trip to Saudi Arabia and Qatar.
NPR's Michelle Kellerman reports he is accusing the Trump administration of covering up the
damage.
In a video news conference after returning to Washington, Senator Murphy says he visited
the U.S. Embassy in Riyadh, which was damaged in drone attacks early in the war, and he saw
the damage to Qatar's energy infrastructure.
But the Pentagon would not allow him to see U.S. military bases, and he calls that absolutely

This is a really dangerous moment when the administration is giving its middle finger

Michelle Kellerman, NPR News, the State Department.

Hegseth says Nidal Hassan's death will be live-streamed in early December.
Hassan killed 13 people at Fort Hood in 2009.
A new survey shows a growing number of Medicare recipients use artificial intelligence to
compare plans during open enrollment this month.
NPR's Windsor Johnston reports scams and inaccurate information could put those shopping for coverage
at risk.
The survey by eHealth found 61 percent of Medicare beneficiaries plan to use AI to compare coverage.
Whitney Stenham is the company's vice president of consumer enablement.
She says AI can help explain confusing terms but may lack current information about which
doctors and prescriptions a plan covers.
She also warns shoppers about suspicious calls.
An unexpected caller calls and asks you for your Medicare number or financial information
and pressures you for immediate action.
Hang up and verify who you're dealing with.
She also recommends verifying AI's answers directly with Medicare or the insurance company.
Windsor Johnston, NPR News.
